record.original_question: Suppose that a billiard table has a sequence of convex causti cs with rotation numbers converging to some number omega ∈ (0, 1/2). Does it imply that the table is an ellipse? The previously discussed rotation numbers, 0 and 1 /2, are clearly special. One may generalize the notion of caustic for higher-dimensional billiar ds as a hypersurface such that if a segment of the billiard trajectory is tangent to it, then the refle cted segment is again tangent to this hypersurface. However, this notion is very restrictive: if the dimension of the Euclidean space is at least three, the only convex billiard table that possess caustics a re ellipsoids [10, 98].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a strictly convex planar domain with smooth boundary $\Gamma = \partial \Omega$, and consider the associated Birkhoff billiard: a point particle moves inside $\Omega$ along straight lines and reflects off $\Gamma$ according to the law of equal angles. A smooth convex curve $\gamma \subset \Omega$ is called a (convex) caustic of the billiard in $\Omega$ if every billiard trajectory tangent to $\gamma$ remains tangent to $\gamma$ after each reflection. To each convex caustic $\gamma$ one associates a rotation number $\rho(\gamma) \in (0, 1/2)$, defined as the limiting average fraction of the perimeter of $\Gamma$ traversed per reflection by any trajectory tangent to $\gamma$.

Question: Suppose that the billiard table $\Omega$ admits a sequence of convex caustics $\{\gamma_n\}_{n \ge 1}$ whose rotation numbers $\rho(\gamma_n)$ converge to some number $\omega \in (0, 1/2)$. Must $\Gamma$ then be an ellipse?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a generalization of the classical Birkhoff–Poritsky conjecture. Partial results are known: if the sequence of rotation numbers tends to 1/2, the table must be an ellipse (a result by Avila–De Simoi–Kaloshin and related work), and for centrally symmetric tables with a foliation of caustics with rotation numbers in (0,1/4] the conclusion holds (Bialy–Mironov, Annals 2022). For a general accumulation value ω ∈ (0,1/2) the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Birkhoff-Poritsky conjecture for centrally-symmetric billiard tables
status_evidence.snippet: If a neighborhood of the boundary of a centrally symmetric billiard table is foliated by convex caustics of rotation numbers in (0,1/4], then the boundary is an ellipse.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on the Birkhoff–Poritsky conjecture, restricted to specific ranges of rotation numbers and to centrally symmetric tables.

status_evidence.title: On the integrability of Birkhoff billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing the Birkhoff conjecture and remaining open cases for caustics with general rotation numbers.
status_evidence.claim: General version with arbitrary accumulation of rotation numbers in (0,1/2) is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Integrable Billiards and Related Topics
status_evidence.snippet: Recent survey describing the state of the Birkhoff conjecture and related questions on caustics and rotation numbers.
status_evidence.claim: Lists the general convergence-of-rotation-numbers question as still open.
